description: Hey everyone! We are Cosmicode, a crew of enthusiastic first-year CSE engineering students diving into our first hackathon adventure. We blend fresh logic with creative UI thinking, focusing on web development, interactive design, and building immersive space apps We are looking for passionate teammates who bring skills in coding, UI/UX design, data storytelling, or creative problem-solving If you love space tech, clean code, and building cool things under pressure, let's team up and launch this
summary:
SOLAR COMMAND is an interactive 3D space mission design and piloting game that lets players experience the real-world engineering trade-offs behind interplanetary exploration. Designed for solo players or a three-person Mission Control team (Flight Director, Systems Engineer, and Science Lead), participants begin in a Vehicle Hangar comparing historic and modern launch systems—including the Space Shuttle, Falcon Heavy, and NASA SLS—before configuring their spacecraft.

Players must balance strict constraints across budget, payload mass, net power, communications, and fuel capacity. Realistic physics rules enforce engineering logic: the Space Shuttle cannot escape Low Earth Orbit, outer-planet missions require RTG nuclear power where sunlight is too weak for solar arrays, and heavy payloads require high-lift rockets.

Once launched, players manually pilot their spacecraft across a 3D Solar System using keyboard controls, docking at Orbital Fuel Stations to refuel, surviving solar storm votes, and braking safely to deploy satellites and landers. By turning complex systems engineering into hands-on gameplay, SOLAR COMMAND makes space mission architecture accessible and engaging for learners of all backgrounds.
details:
SOLAR COMMAND is a browser-based 3D interplanetary mission design and orbital piloting simulator built for solo learners or a three-person Mission Control team (Flight Director, Systems Engineer, and Science Lead). Players progress through four interactive stages:

  1. Vehicle Hangar: Compare historic and modern launch vehicles—Space Shuttle, Falcon Heavy, and NASA SLS Block 2—alongside their payload capacities and orbital limits.
  2. Spacecraft & Subsystem Engineering: Select any destination across all 8 planets (Mercury through Neptune) and configure power systems, drop-tank fuel extensions, Deep Space Network telemetry dishes, and science payloads (atmospheric scanners and planetary landers) within a strict $300M budget, mass ceiling, and net-power balance.
  3. Manual 3D Piloting & Orbital Refueling: Pilot the spacecraft across a 3D Solar System using keyboard controls (W A S D / Arrow keys). Players must manage momentum, steer around non-target planets, dock inside glowing green Orbital Fuel Stations (Propellant Depots) to replenish fuel on deep-space transits, vote on mid-mission Solar Storm events, and fire retro-brakes to decelerate below 22 km/s for safe arrival—all while protecting a 3-Life hull integrity system.
  4. Planetary Arrival & Dossier: Upon safe arrival, a custom 3D satellite enters live orbit around the target planet alongside real missions (ISS, Hubble, MRO, Juno) and unlocks an official planetary science dossier and team performance rank.

Engineering Factors Considered

  • Realistic Physics & Constraints: The Space Shuttle is restricted to Low Earth Orbit (LEO) and cannot escape Earth's gravity well; outer-planet missions (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune) require RTG Nuclear Power because solar irradiance is too weak; and high-speed impacts (> 22 km/s) or wrong-planet collisions damage the spacecraft.
  • Accessibility & Zero Setup: Engineered as a lightweight, single-file web application so students and judges can launch and play immediately on any computer without installing software.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Languages & Web Standards: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+)
  • 3D Graphics & Audio: Three.js (r128 WebGL) for 3D planetary orbits, lighting, and kinematics; native Web Audio API for procedural thruster, refueling, and alert sound synthesis
  • Development & Deployment: Visual Studio Code, GitHub, and Netlify CDN for public cloud hosting

Benefits & Intended Impact Traditional space science education often relies on passive diagrams that hide the real trade-offs aerospace engineers face. SOLAR COMMAND transforms orbital mechanics, delta-v budgeting, and systems engineering into collaborative, hands-on gameplay—inspiring students and lifelong learners to explore how NASA plans and executes deep-space missions.
